//: Composite indexes for the feed. Firestore will serve each of the feed's four queries from a single-field index only if the filter and the order are on the same field, which none of them are: the home feed filters on visibility, userId or visibleToUids and orders by createdAt. Without these the listeners fail with FAILED_PRECONDITION / 'The query requires an index'. Deploy with: firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes

indexes.//: Public posts, newest first. Also serves the legacy query: Firestore's `== null` matches a missing field, and a null filter with an order on a different field needs its own index.
Your own posts, newest first. Needed whichever way round the two fields are combined.
Restricted posts you are in the audience of, newest first.

A profile's public posts, newest first. The feed's public query plus an equality on the author: two equality filters with an order on a third field cannot be served by any single-field index, so this triple is its own index.
A profile's restricted posts that the viewer is in the audience of. Same shape as the restricted feed with the author narrowed onto it.

The inbox. `array-contains` on participants combined with an order on a different field cannot be served by a single-field index, so this pair needs its own. The listener also has to pair it with the participants filter in the rules: without the filter the rules cannot be validated and the read is refused.
Pinned messages: pinned equality filter + createdAt order. This query on chats/{chatId}/messages needs a composite index.
